questions.question: 用 cache-aside 模式时，写操作更新完数据库后，为什么标准做法是删除缓存里的 key，而不是把新值写进缓存？
options: 更新会让 LRU 把这个 key 提到最近访问的位置，挤掉真正的热点数据
并发写可能乱序更新缓存，使其停在旧值；删除后由下次读回填
删除能把缓存和数据库之间的不一致窗口彻底降到零，更新做不到
删除比更新少一次序列化和网络往返，写延迟更低，这是主要的考虑
questions.explanation: A 写 v1、B 写 v2，B 先更新缓存、A 后更新，缓存就永远停在 v1；删除则把「该存什么」交给下一次读数据库。但删除也不能让不一致窗口归零：删完立刻有人读，仍可能回填旧值，所以才有延迟双删，而且必须给业务定好能容忍多旧的数据。
questions.question_en: In the cache-aside pattern, after a write updates the database, why is the standard practice to delete the cache key rather than write the new value into the cache?
options_en: Updating makes LRU treat the key as recently used, pushing out the data that is actually hot
Concurrent writes can land out of order and strand a stale value; deleting lets the next read refill it
Deleting shrinks the inconsistency window between cache and database to zero, which updating cannot do
Deleting saves a serialization step and a network round trip, so write latency is lower; that is the main reason
questions.explanation_en: If A writes v1 and B writes v2, but B updates the cache before A does, the cache is stuck on v1 for good. Deleting leaves the question of what to cache to the next database read. Deleting doesn't close the inconsistency window either: a read right after the delete can still refill a stale value, which is why delayed double-delete exists and why the business must set an explicit staleness tolerance.

questions.question: 大促前夜批量预热了几十万个商品缓存，TTL 都设成 3600 秒。一小时后数据库突然被打爆，过了一会儿又恢复。这是哪类问题，对应的解法是什么？
options: LRU 被一次性批量写入污染，改用带准入控制的 W-TinyLFU
单个热 key 过期引发的击穿，用 single-flight 只放一个请求回源
大批 key 同一时刻过期的雪崩，给 TTL 加随机抖动错开过期时间
大量请求查不存在的 key 的穿透，用 Bloom Filter 在前面拦截
questions.explanation: 同一批写入、同一个 TTL，就会同一时刻集体过期，这是雪崩，解法是在 TTL 上加随机抖动，比如 3600 加 0 到 300 秒的随机值。击穿说的是单个热 key 过期，single-flight 能挡住同一个 key 的并发回源，却挡不住几十万个不同 key 同时失效。
questions.question_en: The night before a big sale, hundreds of thousands of product entries are pre-warmed into the cache, all with a TTL of 3,600 seconds. An hour later the database is suddenly overwhelmed, then recovers after a while. What kind of problem is this, and what is the fix?
options_en: LRU pollution from a one-off bulk write; switch to W-TinyLFU with admission control
A thundering herd from one hot key expiring; use single-flight so only one request goes to the database
A cache avalanche from many keys expiring at the same moment; add random jitter to the TTLs to spread out expiry
Cache penetration from requests for nonexistent keys; put a Bloom filter in front to block them
questions.explanation_en: Keys written together with the same TTL all expire together: that's an avalanche, fixed by adding random jitter to the TTL, e.g. 3600 plus a random 0 to 300 seconds. A thundering herd involves a single hot key; single-flight collapses concurrent misses on one key but can't help when hundreds of thousands of different keys expire at once.

questions.question: 一个用 LRU 淘汰的缓存，平时命中率很高；某天有爬虫把全站页面挨个抓了一遍，之后命中率大跌，热门内容反复回源。以下哪种分析最准确？
options: 根源是缓存容量不够；只要容量能装下全站页面，换什么淘汰策略都无关紧要
这是 LFU 式的旧数据沉淀，新热点进不来；应给访问计数加衰减，或者换回 LRU
LRU 扫描抗性差，一次性访问挤走了热点；W-TinyLFU 的准入控制能挡住它们
爬虫请求的大多是不存在的页面，属于缓存穿透；应缓存空值，或加 Bloom Filter
questions.explanation: LRU 只看最近有没有被访问，一次性扫描会把大量只用一次的 key 推到最新的位置，把真正的热点挤出去，这就是扫描抗性差。旧热点沉淀、新热点进不来是 LFU 的毛病，症状正好相反；W-TinyLFU 用 Count-Min Sketch 估计频率，让稀有 key 进不了缓存。
questions.question_en: A cache using LRU eviction normally has a high hit rate. One day a crawler fetches every page on the site once, and afterward the hit rate collapses and popular content keeps missing. Which diagnosis is most accurate?
options_en: The root cause is insufficient capacity; if the cache held the whole site, the eviction policy wouldn't matter
This is LFU-style stale entries piling up so new hot items can't get in; add decay to the access counts, or switch back to LRU
LRU has poor scan resistance, so one-off hits flushed the hot set; W-TinyLFU's admission filter blocks them
The crawler mostly requested nonexistent pages, which is cache penetration; cache the empty results or add a Bloom filter
questions.explanation_en: LRU only tracks recency, so a one-time scan pushes a flood of single-use keys to the front and evicts the real hot set; that's poor scan resistance. Old hot items settling in and blocking new ones is LFU's weakness, the opposite symptom. W-TinyLFU estimates frequency with a Count-Min Sketch and refuses admission to rarely seen keys.
